name: N,n-dimethylurea
description: N,N-Dimethylurea (CAS 598-94-7 ), also recognized commercially as 1,1-dimethylurea and asym-Dimethylurea, is a substituted urea derivative used across pharmaceutical synthesis, agrochemical production, and polymer chemistry. It functions primarily as a solvent, reaction intermediate, and plasticizing agent in industrial formulations. In pharmaceutical and biotechnology manufacturing, it serves as a solvent and carrier in synthesis routes. This compound is preferred where standard urea would introduce unwanted reactivity. Agrochemical formulators use it as a building block in the production of herbicides and plant growth regulators, particularly within the phenylurea class. In polymer and resin systems, it acts as a plasticizer and softener, improving flexibility and processability in certain thermoset formulations. It also finds use in buffering and pH-control applications. These applications are common within biological media and research-grade formulations. The product is supplied as a white crystalline solid or powder, ensuring ease of handling during the manufacturing process. Technical and research grades are the most commonly available, with purity levels typically ranging from 98% to 99%+ for synthesis and laboratory applications. This ensures high performance in sensitive chemical reactions. Packaging options generally range from small quantities for R&D use to bulk quantities for industrial procurement.
